verdict.why: Option X is more faithful to the order and more consistently buildable. Design 1 reviews the spec loop, research, council, later stages and residual HTTP call sites. Designs 2-3 and C1-C3 turn the meanings/text split into concrete role resolution, validated meanings, revisions, hashes, coverage tags and gap handling, without inventing Option Y's size-S exemption (Y D2) or its L-only limitation for plan decisions (Y D6). X Design 4, REQ-4 and T9-T10 enforce literally one HTTP request per validator; Y C4/D9/R7 explicitly permit a second attempt after a transport failure, contradicting the owner's 'one request each'. X Design 5 and C5-C6 provide the stronger accounting architecture: one HTTP egress module, a row for successful, failed and timed-out calls, explicit BYOK/upstream branches, and append-preserving --judge-only behaviour. Y D17/C6 omit calls returning no usage, while Y D15 generalizes the single measured BYOK case into c+u whenever c<u, risking double-counted ordinary calls. X Design 6/C7 also give Observatory a concrete summary.json contract and retain a local warning path when provider data lags or is unavailable. Option Y has two notable advantages: D10 resolves the judge directly from the thinker role, and D28/R15 provide a more demanding blind quality replay. Those do not outweigh its validator, ledger and cost-rule deviations.
risks: X is internally contradictory about the council cap: REQ-12 says the thinker is never skipped for money, but Design 4 and T22 skip the judge when the panel exceeds the cap. That can leave a round without the required Fable verdict; the judge should run whenever the verdict quorum exists, with overrun reported separately.

X Design 4/C4 checks the configured judge against roles.thinker only after the round. A misconfiguration can therefore purchase the wrong judge call before failing; Y's direct role resolution is the safer design.

X REQ-14/Rollout 6 measures quality but does not establish a firm remediation or rollback outcome when it regresses; the default remains 'keep the split'. The ID/tag checks also establish textual coverage, not semantic fidelity, so writer drift still depends substantially on the council and canary.

X's null-cost recovery edge case is inconsistent: spend.py record appends a manual row, but spend.py check would continue rejecting the original status-ok null-cost row. An amendment or supersession rule is needed.

The role map, meanings schema, ledger and summary contracts are extensive for an M-sized change. Rollout should preserve X's staged implementation and real BYOK/Observatory fixtures rather than treating all the new machinery as independently proven.
